  "summary": "A broad workplace umbrella for adult {{user}} and adult {{char}}. One may be a new hire, transfer, long-time coworker, rival, boss, trainee, mentor, or partner on different shifts. Their connection can remain professional, become friendship, rivalry, mentoring, mutual dependence, or potentially romance. The source treats industry, role, hierarchy, schedule, workplace policy, career goals, and conflicts of interest as real structural variables rather than background decoration.",
  "core_premise": "The engine is repeated adult contact through work. The workplace creates routines, dependence, hierarchy, shared problems, training, handovers, travel, overtime, and career consequences that shape how two people know each other. Personal closeness may change work, but work remains a real institution with safety, fairness, privacy, and power boundaries. Romance is one possible trajectory, not the default destination.",
  "setup": "Begin close to a meaningful workplace moment: a new-hire introduction, first shift together, transfer, handover, rivalry result, overtime period, trip departure, training assignment, roster change, promotion, resignation, or after-work transition. Establish job roles, hierarchy, industry, and enough workplace context for the relationship dynamic to make sense. Do not pre-write {{user}}'s attraction, friendship, consent, promotion choice, resignation, confrontation, or career decision.",

  "generation_rules": [
    "Preserve the broad workplace umbrella: adult {{user}} and adult {{char}} know each other through shared work, and the workplace materially shapes the scenario.",
    "If New Hire is selected, clearly establish who is new and who already knows the workplace.",
    "If Department Transfer is selected, preserve that one adult already knows the organization but is new to the immediate team/site/role.",
    "If Long-Time Coworkers is selected, use accumulated professional history, routines, trust, or assumptions rather than treating them like strangers.",
    "If Office Rival is selected, define the actual professional competition and avoid turning rivalry into automatic romance.",
    "If My Boss is selected, make managerial power real and preserve a strict separation between employment decisions and romantic/sexual consent.",
    "If After Work is selected, move meaningful personal interaction outside active work duties without assuming romance.",
    "If Business Trip is selected, preserve work purpose, travel logistics, separate consent, and ordinary accommodation/privacy boundaries.",
    "If Overtime is selected, explain why extra work is happening and avoid treating an unlocked workplace as forced confinement.",
    "If Different Shifts is selected, make handovers, rare overlap, rosters, and schedule changes central.",
    "If Trainee Train Drivers / Training Together is selected, preserve adult trainee status, rules/safety learning, assessments, simulations, route knowledge, and formal instructors/assessors.",
    "Do not force romance, sexual tension, dating, marriage, rivalry, friendship, or breakup as the inevitable trajectory.",
    "Do not write {{user}}'s attraction, consent, dialogue, career decision, resignation, promotion response, or personal boundaries as settled fact.",
    "Treat workplace gossip and coworker assumptions as perspective rather than truth.",
    "Keep professional competence and career goals intact even when romance develops.",
    "If a selected preset narrows industry, hierarchy, role, schedule, dynamic, or outcome, preserve it while varying remaining axes."

    "Rejecting personal interest must not trigger workplace retaliation.",
    "Do not treat managerial, trainer, assessor, owner, client, or senior-specialist authority as romantic consent.",
    "If direct reporting or assessment creates a conflict of interest, allow disclosure, reassignment, delay, or non-pursuit as valid outcomes.",
